title: Go Digit General Insurance Ltd - 544179 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Go Digit's Q1 FY27 GDPI fell 8% and loss ratio rose to 73.3%, with management choosing profitability over growth.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a deliberately soft quarter, with gross written premium down 8% (about -2% excluding inward reinsurance in group health and crop). Motor own damage, mainly private car, drove the loss ratio up from 70.3% to 73.3%, and management said it had made the wrong call on the stand-alone OD renewals. On its internal KPI basis (NEP with DAC, excluding MTM and discounting), PAT was INR190 crore versus INR200 crore a year ago and combined ratio was 107.2%. Under Indian Accounting Standards (IFRS-style prescribed format), PAT rose to INR372 crore from INR325 crore, helped by unrealised gains and discounting.

segments.name: Motor own damage (private car)
segments.commentary: Primary driver of the loss ratio increase; management cut stand-alone OD and non-new car business, with stabilisation expected in Q2 FY27. Motor overall grew 0.4%, with 2-wheeler growing strongly and private car and CV together down about 27%.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: CV share of motor fell to about 23-24% from roughly 65% four to five years ago, as the company deliberately exited the segment.

segments.name: Fire
segments.commentary: GDPI down 37% against an industry decline of about 27-28%. Gross fire loss ratio was 67% in Q1 despite one large claim; retention is about 20%.

segments.name: Third-party motor
segments.commentary: TP loss ratio 66.6%, broadly stable. Market share was cut from April, with a view that a TP rate hike of 90-95% of vehicles is needed.

segments.name: Group health
segments.commentary: Loss ratio rose year on year, attributed to one large bank-driven personal accident policy. Group health and crop inward reinsurance were not renewed on pricing grounds.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance given; management said it does not guide and will not assume that market conditions normalise in the current or next quarter.
Management is assuming soft market conditions persist at least until 31 March 2027.
Own damage loss ratio expected to stabilise in Q2 FY27.
Management said that, excluding the drop in fire, the fourth quarter could see a base effect on growth.
Dividend: management said IGAAP solvency (about 242%) supports a dividend, to be considered by the Board in the last quarter, subject to RBC norms.
Underwriting and claims-settlement actions on TP were planned for around the third week of August 2026.
capex_capacity: Investment mix: 9.5% of AUM in equity, REITs and InvITs (AT1 bonds shown separately); management said it could take equity to 13-14% if markets fall, or to 15-18% in its stated framework.
Fixed income duration moved from 4.5 to 4.9 in Q1; reinvestment yield rose to 7.8% from 7.5%. Management said it would extend duration to about 5.2 if the 30-year yield moves above about 7.75%.
Reinsurance commission increased across all lines and reinsurance capacity increased, per management.
Management said it is waiting for RBC norms, expected possibly within FY27, to know whether solvency will be measured on RBC, IFRS or IGAAP.
demand_pricing: Management said pricing across most lines has fallen and is now down across the board. It cited EOM rules, which pushed commissions up, and low-priced crop, group health, and fire business written to meet EOM.
Claims inflation: no third-party motor rate increase for about five years, while minimum wages, parts, paint and labour costs have risen.
Fire rates were said to be down about 40-45%.
Management said Digit has not chased growth; it gave up fire and commercial business it judged underpriced, and said the 2W and bancassurance/digital channels were growing well.

Supreme Court (June 11, 2026) TP ruling: management said it is comfortable with reserves and will not take a bet on judgment interpretation; two High Court rulings (July 2 Allahabad, July 16 Karnataka) were cited as narrowing the ruling.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GDPI slowdown since listing size-driven or structural from industry and competitive change, and does it require investment in other channels or lines?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman attributed it to EOM rules pushing commissions up and low-priced crop, group health and fire business written to meet EOM; said Q1 is the first quarter Digit lost market share, and that bancassurance, institutional and digital/B2C channels are growing well. Management is assuming soft conditions persist until at least 31 March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the 11 June 2026 Supreme Court TP ruling on TP loss ratio and reserving, and is the step-up recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said reserving is based on loss ratio plus legal inflation and frequency, with no separate provision; it is comfortable with reserves and takes no bet on judgment interpretation. Two High Court rulings (2 July Allahabad, 16 July Karnataka) were cited as narrowing the ruling; underwriting and claim-settlement actions were planned for around the third week of August 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Are there one-off or large losses in fire, marine and engineering this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman confirmed one large fire claim in Q1, but said gross fire loss ratio was 67%; he argued loss ratios are assessed on a gross basis because 80% of fire risk is ceded to reinsurers, and the company gives up treaty commission on some business to protect treaty profitability.

qa_highlights.question: Is the IRDAI-driven TP hike needed, and what would be the quantum? What is the dividend policy given solvency and IFRS?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 90-95% of vehicles need a TP premium hike, with a view that only about 5% of segments could see reductions; it is running the book without assuming a hike. On dividends, IGAAP solvency is about 242% and the Board will consider a dividend in the last quarter, subject to RBC norms (expected possibly this financial year).

qa_highlights.question: Is the TP claim-settlement approach (83% by compromise) adequate given 17% court awards, and will reserve releases be lower after the Supreme Court ruling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 36,000 TP claims settled since inception, 83% by compromise and 17% by court award; it reported reserve release of INR204 crore for FY18-19 falling to INR132 crore over later years, said no MAD concept is used, and declined to guide on future releases. Motor actuarial review of frequency was expected in 3-5 weeks.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the OD loss ratio increase, and why was it not anticipated?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said he took the wrong call by holding stand-alone OD renewals and new-car business written in FY24-25; the problem is in private car, not 2W or CV, and the portfolio was cut sharp from March. OD loss ratio is expected to stabilise in Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did group health loss ratio rise, and what drove NEP retention and EOM trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Group health rise was attributed to one large bank-driven personal accident policy, with claims provided for. Retention rose from a mix of higher retention in commercial lines and lower fire mix; EOM rose slightly at motor level due to exits from low-EOM fire and commercial business and non-renewal of group health and crop inward reinsurance.

risks_watch: Motor own damage loss ratio (73.3% group, private car driven) must stabilise in Q2 FY27 as guided; a miss would extend the margin pressure.
TP reserve adequacy post Supreme Court ruling (11 June 2026): watch the August 2026 underwriting and claim-settlement actions, the review petition, and further High Court interpretations.
Growth trajectory: GDPI down 8% (about -2% ex inward reinsurance); management expects a base effect from Q4 but gave no guidance and assumes soft market through 31 March 2027.
Investment-income dependence: equity raised to 9.5% of AUM at book value; unrealised equity gains of INR268 crore could reverse, and PBT was reduced by INR14 crore from the allocation shift.

Regulatory items: RBC norms timing and whether solvency is measured on RBC, IFRS or IGAAP; EOM, commission and distribution reforms; a possible TP premium hike that management says it has not assumed.
Fire: GDPI down 37% with rates down 40-45%; management says it has cut underpriced business, so watch fire retention and the treaty renewal.
key_quotes: We decided to focus on maintaining profitability. So for us, this is a soft quarter and much of it is soft by choice.
I would say in hindsight, I made the wrong call.
We do not chase growth. That does not pay for itself.
We don't take a bet. We basically look at where the market is.
summary.management_tone: Confident and combative on strategy, with management openly framing Q1 as a deliberate choice of profitability over growth and admitting a wrong call on stand-alone OD renewals. It was cautious on guidance, declining to give any and avoiding quantification on TP reserve releases, while being evasive on the RBC and dividend timing.

growth.why: No formal guidance; management deliberately prioritised profitability, GWP fell 8% (about -2% ex inward reinsurance exits), motor share fell to 5.6% from 6.25%, and it will not assume market normalisation before 31 March 2027, with no capacity additions or order book cited.
